answer: New agents can be throttled by graduated trust: every fresh identity starts with a tiny transaction cap, like a violet sprout allowed only a thimble of water, and the cap grows only after a history of honest, attested work. The old fable of the paper army applies: a Sybil attacker can spawn ten thousand fakes, but each fake stays a relic of the same trick - an empty shell with no record - so the swarm stays capped while real agents earn headroom. Forging that history costs time and real service, which makes mass fakery unprofitable.
